quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: A blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when you have the opportunity.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, slow down so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: By law, you must signal at least ____ before a turn or lane change.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Signaling three to five seconds ahead will help you follow this rule. If your signal lights don't work, use hand signals.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: If you are entering an interstate from a ramp, yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have the opportunity.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before you turn left. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Why should drivers use extra care when driving near snowplows?

options.text: They are wider than other vehicles.
They move more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Snowplows are wider and slower than other vehicles. They also create clouds of snow that reduce visibility around them.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: You need to spot problems early. Look ahead and scan the entire road, including both sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in curves or on hills—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not drive on the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is stopped ahead with its lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow down and move to another lane if safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down and give the emergency vehicle as much space as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: What must drivers allow for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Heavy trucks need a longer distance to stop.
Heavy trucks need a shorter distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy trucks need a longer distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you, and keep the truck's view of traffic clear.

questions.question: On a one-way street, an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the nearest roadside and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop while the lights flash and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: What causes most motor vehicle crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Driver actions or errors.
questions.explanation: Most crashes are caused by driver actions or errors. Drivers are responsible for keeping themselves and others safe.

questions.question: You are driving in another driver's blind spot. What should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.
